chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskhan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A mature woman (thayyib) proposes marriage to herself.' He said: 'She has more authority over herself; she may appoint her affair to whomever she wishes, and there is no harm in that, after she has been married to a husband previously.'

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِنَفْسِهَا: She has more authority over herself
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ الثَّيِّبُ: A mature woman who has previously been married
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: And there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Does a mature woman need a male guardian to contract her own marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a *thayyib* (mature woman who has previously been married) retains full autonomy over her marriage contract, distinguishing her status from that of a *bikr* (virgin) who typically requires a guardian's consent. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that her prior marital experience grants her the legal capacity (*ahliyyah*) to appoint any representative she chooses for her *nikah*, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on female agency in family law.
